title: Trail Cameras Show Coyotes Using the World’s Largest Wildlife Crossing - Nautilus
author: David Nield
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEnvironmentTrail Cameras Show Coyotes Using the World’s Largest Wildlife CrossingIt officially opens next monthDNBy David Nield7:00 AM CST on November 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe new Wallis Annenberg Wildlife Crossing, a bridge that connects two portions of Callifornia’s Santa Monica Mountains separated by 10 lanes of highway, has its first beneficiaries: A coyote used it to cross the 101 freeway on October 28th, and a few days later, a second coyote did the same.Powered By 1060.9K 00ShareNextStayThe crossing, which measures around 210 feet in length and 174 feet in width, isn’t finished yet, with the official opening scheduled for December, but it’s encouraging that it’s already helping animals get from point A to point B without having to risk their lives getting through L.A. traffic. The $114 million project will also include a second wildlife bridge and 13 acres of restored habitat. It connects the Simi Hills in the north to the Santa Monica Mountains in the south.The crossing under construction. Credit: Wallis Annenberg Wildlife CrossingSubscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
